Dickens’s passage emphasizes contradictions and extremes — “best of times” and “worst of times,” “season of Light” and “season of Darkness” — suggesting a cynical view of the Revolution’s chaotic and polarized nature.  
Wordsworth’s lines, by contrast, express a sense of exhilaration and idealism — “Bliss was it in that dawn to be alive” — indicating an enthusiastic, hopeful perspective.  

Final answer: (C)
